# Crontinel docs

> Documentation for Crontinel, monitoring for cron jobs, queues, workers, and background tasks.

## Start

- [Docs home](https://docs.crontinel.com/): Documentation for installing and operating Crontinel

## check-in

- [Check-in from any runtime](https://docs.crontinel.com/check-in/recipes/): Five first-class runtimes post one HTTP outcome receipt — curl, Node, Python, Sidekiq, and GitHub Actions. Laravel is the deep package path.

## Guides

- [Billing & Plans](https://docs.crontinel.com/billing/): What the Free, Pro, and Team plans include: how many apps, how long history is kept, and how to upgrade off the free tier.
- [FAQ](https://docs.crontinel.com/faq/): Whether you need an account, how Crontinel behaves with Octane, what data the package sends, and what happens if the hosted app is down.
- [Installation](https://docs.crontinel.com/installation/): Start with the HTTP outcome receipt from any runtime. On Laravel, install crontinel/laravel for schedule attach, queue depth, and Horizon.
- [Introduction](https://docs.crontinel.com/introduction/): Crontinel tells you when a background job finished without doing the work. Check in from curl, Node, Python, Sidekiq, or GitHub Actions. Laravel adds schedule, queue, and Horizon evidence.
- [Quick Start](https://docs.crontinel.com/quick-start/): Send one HTTP outcome receipt from any runtime, then optionally install the Laravel package for schedule, queue, and Horizon.
- [Security](https://docs.crontinel.com/security/): Lock down the Crontinel dashboard, verify webhook signatures, and protect sensitive operational data in your Laravel application.
- [Self-Hosting](https://docs.crontinel.com/self-hosting/): Run the Crontinel hosted stack on a server you control when you don't want the dashboard to live only on app.crontinel.com.
- [Status Pages](https://docs.crontinel.com/status-page/): Give your users a public status page showing real-time uptime, incident history, and per-monitor health, included free with every Crontinel account.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.crontinel.com/troubleshooting/): Fixes for common Crontinel issues with the dashboard, cron monitor, queue monitor, Horizon, alerts, CLI, and SaaS connection
- [Upgrading](https://docs.crontinel.com/upgrading/): How to move between Crontinel versions, including breaking changes and which config keys you need to update after the upgrade.

## SDKs

- [SDKs & Packages](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/): HTTP check-in is the path for every runtime. The Laravel package is the maintained deep integration. Other language repos are not a support claim until they send the outcome receipt and have an owner.
- [CLI / Docker](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/cli/): Use the Crontinel CLI to send a success or failure ping after a cron job, Docker container, or Kubernetes CronJob finishes.
- [.NET](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/dotnet/): Install the Crontinel .NET SDK and report cron and background job runs from a .NET application to your Crontinel dashboard.
- [Go](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/go/): Install crontinel/go and report cron and background job runs from a Go app to a hosted or self-hosted Crontinel dashboard.
- [Laravel](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/laravel/): Deep Laravel package for schedule attach, queue depth, and Horizon. Outcome receipts still use the same HTTP body as every other runtime.
- [Node.js / TypeScript](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/node/): Prefer the HTTP check-in recipe for Node. The npm package is not a supported outcome-receipt path until it has a maintenance owner.
- [PHP](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/php/): Install crontinel/php and report cron and background job runs from a PHP application that does not use the Laravel package.
- [Python](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/python/): Prefer the HTTP check-in recipe for Python. The PyPI package is not a supported outcome-receipt path until it has a maintenance owner.
- [Ruby on Rails](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/rails/): Install crontinel-rails so ActiveJob and scheduled jobs are reported to Crontinel without a manual heartbeat in each job.
- [Ruby](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/ruby/): Install the Crontinel Ruby gem and report cron and background job runs from a Ruby application to your Crontinel dashboard.
- [Rust](https://docs.crontinel.com/sdks/rust/): Install crontinel-rust and report cron and background job runs from a Rust app to a hosted or self-hosted Crontinel dashboard.

## Monitors

- [Cron Monitor](https://docs.crontinel.com/monitors/cron/): Record every scheduled command's exit code and duration, including runs that fail while the scheduler process itself stays up.
- [Horizon Monitor](https://docs.crontinel.com/monitors/horizon/): Read Laravel Horizon supervisor status, paused queues, and worker health from inside the app, instead of checking whether a URL returns 200.
- [Queue Monitor](https://docs.crontinel.com/monitors/queues/): Watch Laravel queue depth, failed jobs, and wait time, and see when a queue climbs or a worker stops processing new jobs.

## Alerts

- [Alert Channels](https://docs.crontinel.com/alerts/channels/): Send Crontinel alerts to Slack, email, or a webhook when a cron run fails, a queue climbs, or a Horizon supervisor stops.
- [CLI Health Check](https://docs.crontinel.com/alerts/cli/): Run php artisan crontinel:check in CI or from an external monitor so a failed cron or a stalled queue fails the pipeline.

## AI clients

- [AI Agent Monitoring](https://docs.crontinel.com/mcp/ai-agent-monitoring/): Planned feature. Not available in a released package yet.
- [Claude Code Setup](https://docs.crontinel.com/mcp/claude-code/): Add the Crontinel MCP server to Claude Code so the assistant can read cron, queue, and Horizon status without leaving the editor.
- [MCP Integration Overview](https://docs.crontinel.com/mcp/overview/): Connect an AI assistant to Crontinel with the Model Context Protocol and read cron, queue, and Horizon status from the editor.
- [Available MCP Tools](https://docs.crontinel.com/mcp/tools/): MCP tools for listing scheduled jobs, reading a cron run, checking queue depth and Horizon, and creating or dismissing alerts.

## Agent

- [Agent Guide](https://docs.crontinel.com/agent/guide/): The Crontinel agent is a daemon on your server. It runs only allowlisted commands from the dashboard and reports the result.

## Reference

- [REST API Reference](https://docs.crontinel.com/reference/api/): HTTP API for Pro and Team plans. Send a Bearer API key, then list monitors and read recent cron and queue run history from the app.
- [Configuration Reference](https://docs.crontinel.com/reference/configuration/): Environment variables and config keys for the Laravel package, the connection to the hosted app, and a self-hosted install.

## Product

- [Marketing site guide for assistants](https://crontinel.com/llms.txt): Public pages on crontinel.com
- [Hosted app](https://app.crontinel.com/): Sign in to the hosted monitor. Customer data is not part of this guide.
